release_claim.statement: Haxe.Go is a pre-1.0 beta for pinned, application-qualified portable workloads on the admitted toolchain, platform, and operation/member surface.
release_claim.default_disposition: Any unlisted module operation, member, platform, architecture, native API, error path, or trust model is excluded from the admitted release scope.

semantic-diff-supported.meaning: Named deterministic behavior is compared between Haxe --interp and generated Go, which also compiles, passes go test, and runs.

compile-go-test-run-supported.meaning: The named target-sensitive behavior compiles, passes go test, runs on Go, and matches an explicit expected contract without claiming interpreter parity.

compile-only.meaning: The named surface compiles or cross-builds, but runtime and semantic support are not admitted.

experimental.meaning: The named surface is implemented and tested in some lanes but remains outside the admitted release contract.

compatibility-only.meaning: The input or behavior is retained for compatibility and does not define a separate semantic product or release admission.

excluded.meaning: The named surface is deliberately unsupported by the admitted release scope.

platforms.qualification: Canonical beta evidence platform; release evidence must record the exact hosted runner image and resolved toolchain patches.
The quality workflow runs macos-latest, but the architecture and image are not frozen as a release compatibility promise.
exclusions: No stable runner-image or architecture compatibility promise

platforms.qualification: Representative examples cross-build; no release runtime, race, or security matrix is admitted.

platforms.qualification: Representative examples cross-build; the moving macos-latest lane is tracked separately.

platforms.qualification: No implicit operating-system or architecture support is inferred.
exclusions: All combinations not named above

operations.qualification: Get, set, clear, and main/worker isolation have interpreter parity. Runtime churn proves completed portable workers and compiler-owned detached go.Go.spawn callbacks release logical identity and TLS values on return and native-panic unwind; supported Go race, checkptr, vet, and staticcheck lanes exercise the boundary.
exclusions: Automatic lifecycle discovery for goroutines created outside portable Thread and compiler-owned go.Go.spawn boundaries

operations.qualification: Named foreground-thread and event-loop behavior has interpreter parity; deterministic supported-Go stress proves pool admission/shutdown exactly once, failed-worker replacement, cancellation cleanup, wakeup deadline recomputation, and bounded portable identity state.
exclusions: Exact scheduler fairness, concurrent ElasticThreadPool.maxThreadsCount mutation, and arbitrary foreign-goroutine lifecycle discovery

surfaces.scope: Operation-split portable networking; only the explicitly admitted Linux/amd64 member groups below participate in the beta release

operations.qualification: On the portable preset, Linux/amd64, Haxe 4.3.7, and Go 1.25.12 or 1.26.5, the admitted core is blocking IPv4 TCP client I/O to application-controlled, pre-resolved numeric endpoints. Deterministic loopback evidence covers connection, source-owned stream reads and writes with partial-progress preservation, flush, local and peer addresses, and close. Repeated evidence covers close of an already-installed connection interrupting an already-blocked read; lifecycle generations separately prevent older connect or bind work from attaching after close.
exclusions: Hostname and DNS behavior; bind, listen, accept, backlog, and other server behavior
Timeout controls, nonblocking mode, select/readiness, waitForRead, shutdown, and fast-send controls
Close racing an in-progress connect is covered by the lifecycle safety invariant but is not a successful client operation
UDP, TLS, HTTP, IPv6, public or hostile networks, long-running load, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

symbols: haxe.Http/sys.Http header, parameter, postData, and postBytes APIs (plain HTTP numeric IPv4)
operations.qualification: The candidate portable Linux/amd64 core for Haxe 4.3.7 and Go 1.25.12 or 1.26.5 is synchronous direct plain HTTP to application-controlled numeric IPv4 endpoints. It preserves ordered and repeated fields, explicit method/body policy, redirects without following, raw compressed bytes, streamed status/header/Output lifecycle, partial-body failures, status classification, requestUrl throwing, and direct connect/header/response progress deadlines. Resource convergence evidence repeats success, timeout, truncation, cancellation, redirect, compression, and close cases until zero active server connections and bounded goroutine and Linux descriptor deltas are observed. Release admission remains fail-closed until the commit-pinned independent review is adjudicated.
exclusions: Hostnames and DNS, HTTPS, proxies, custom sockets, HTTP/2, public Internet behavior, public trust stores, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64
A fixed in-memory request body write to a peer that stops reading is not covered by the progress-timeout claim
Global request-header line ordering and invalid terminal informational responses below 200 are not admitted

symbols: haxe.Http/sys.Http fileTransfer/fileTransfert with request/customRequest (plain HTTP numeric IPv4)
operations.qualification: The candidate portable Linux/amd64 multipart operation on the pinned Haxe/Go toolchains targets application-controlled numeric IPv4 HTTP endpoints and preserves ordered fields, per-request boundary/content-type agreement, exact declared length, bounded source reads, source-error precedence, caller-thread execution, native sink cancellation, and no generated-Haxe callback after public return. Repeated early-response, timeout, server-close, source-failure, and exact-size cases pass generated-Haxe race and native resource-convergence gates. Release admission remains fail-closed until the commit-pinned independent review is adjudicated.
exclusions: A custom Input.readBytes implementation that blocks forever inside user code cannot be forcibly canceled
Public or hostile peers, indefinite sources, proxies, HTTPS, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: The candidate portable preset's deterministic target-owned data URL path uses the same status, prepare, bounded write, close, and single-error Output choreography as a complete network response. This is a positive haxe.go target contract rather than a claim that Haxe --interp implements data URLs identically. Release admission remains fail-closed until the commit-pinned independent review is adjudicated.
exclusions: Treating this target-owned data URL spelling as an interpreter-wide or cross-target standard

operations.qualification: Focused native and semantic fixtures prove HTTP absolute proxy targets, Go HTTPS CONNECT selection, and typed plain-HTTP custom-socket ownership. This evidence does not bound proxy negotiation or proxy fleet behavior, and HTTPS custom sockets are rejected because the shared socket handle cannot retain TLS identity and verification policy.
exclusions: Proxy negotiation deadlines, proxy authentication fleets, public proxies, HTTPS custom sockets, and custom secure connector policy

operations.qualification: Direct HTTPS currently uses Go's native TLS transport and URL hostname, but the reviewed evidence does not admit public CA-store behavior, HTTP/2, hostile TLS peers, client certificates, proxy composition, or any HTTPS custom-socket path.
exclusions: All HTTPS release behavior, including public trust stores, HTTP/2, hostile peers, client certificates, proxies, custom sockets, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with Haxe 4.3.7 and Go 1.25.12 or 1.26.5, serial plain-TCP server use preserves bind-before-listen, passes each backlog to the OS, accepts blocking IPv4 clients, inherits connected policy, and rolls failed listener transitions back to an empty reusable handle.
exclusions: TLS servers, hostile peers, listener load/soak, same-handle lifecycle races not named here, exact cross-kernel queue counts, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, negative, zero, and positive timeout policy plus blocking/nonblocking mode apply to an already-established plain TCP connection and produce progress, EOF, or Error.Blocked deterministically.
exclusions: Nonblocking connect, DNS work before the socket exists, TLS/UDP controls, hostile peers, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, accept on an already-listening plain TCP socket either returns a connected child or reports Error.Blocked without waiting indefinitely.
exclusions: Nonblocking connect, TLS accept, fairness/load guarantees, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, native plain-TCP read/write/exception readiness preserves caller indexes, buffered bytes, EOF, finite timeouts including snapshot preparation, and duplicate-descriptor ownership.
exclusions: Nonblocking connect, TLS readiness, UDP readiness, high duplicated descriptors beyond the fixed POSIX FdSet capacity, hostile/load behavior, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, established plain TCP supports read/write/both half-close combinations and direct TCP_NODELAY mutation with wire-visible and native option-state evidence.
exclusions: TLS controls, pre-connect concurrent policy mutation, non-TCP transports, hostile/load behavior, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64, Host.localhost returns the operating-system hostname when available or the nonempty literal localhost fallback; exact spelling is environment-dependent.
exclusions: Treating the returned spelling as stable identity or DNS evidence, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: Haxe-compatible named Host construction remains a synchronous OS resolver call before a Socket exists.
exclusions: Timeout, cancellation, resolver selection, search domains, split-horizon behavior, and deterministic external answers

operations.qualification: Reverse lookup remains a synchronous OS resolver operation with environment-dependent results.
exclusions: Timeout, cancellation, resolver selection, and deterministic external answers

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, application-controlled blocking IPv4 datagrams preserve sender identity for empty and nonempty payloads, and failed bind/policy installation retains no descriptor.
exclusions: Inherited TCP connect/listen/accept/shutdown/fast-send, connected UDP, readiness/nonblocking/timeout controls, multicast, IPv6, LAN delivery guarantees, hostile/load behavior, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, setBroadcast applies SO_BROADCAST exactly once to the current or transactionally created IPv4 UDP socket and preserves prior state on failure.
exclusions: LAN broadcast packet delivery, multicast, hostile/load behavior, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

symbols: sys.ssl.Socket.connect (numeric IPv4 route with logical host)
operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, direct application-controlled TLS clients preserve numeric routing versus logical SNI/verification identity, support an application-supplied CA or explicit verification policy, cancel acquisition on close, and detach failed handshakes.
exclusions: Portable public CA stores, public Internet guarantees, client certificates, TLS readiness, hostile peers, indefinite load, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, application-controlled TLS servers retain certificate/SNI policy across bind and listen, and failed accepted handshakes detach and close before the error escapes.
exclusions: Client-certificate authentication, public/hostile peers, handshake-rate/load guarantees, TLS readiness, and runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: On portable Linux/amd64 with the pinned toolchains, TLS close_notify write shutdown preserves reads, TLS read-only shutdown is explicitly unsupported, full shutdown closes the connection, and fast-send reaches TCP_NODELAY through the typed TLS transport.
exclusions: TLS read-only shutdown, which deterministically reports unsupported; TLS readiness; hostile-peer and production-soak behavior; Windows runtime behavior and all runtime support outside Linux/amd64

operations.qualification: Typed snapshots and runtime smokes exist, but the governed native capability matrix is not complete.
exclusions: Stable or complete Go-native collection/error API admission

operations.qualification: Go-specific goroutine and channel lifecycle behavior, including closed-versus-empty receive and native close/send panics, is tested; true native select and the complete public native capability contract remain open.
exclusions: Stable Go concurrency authoring contract

operations.qualification: The named typed extern forms work for covered fixtures; broad callbacks, generics, unsafe shapes, and public API stability remain open.
exclusions: Stable admission of the full extern grammar

trust_assumptions.statement: Application Haxe source, build metadata, extern metadata, and dependency source are reviewed or otherwise trusted.
Repository tooling is installed from the committed npm lock and vendored Reflaxe provenance passes its offline verification.
Admitted file and process operations run on the canonical platform against application-controlled paths and child commands.

Only the named Linux/amd64 IPv4 TCP, UDP, and TLS member groups are admitted. Endpoints, TLS identity/trust, peers, and workloads are application-controlled; HTTP, named/reverse DNS, public networks, hostile-peer guarantees, IPv6, and unlisted operations remain excluded.

known_blockers.scope: Portable HTTP request fidelity, streamed responses, and cancellable uploads
Checksummed same-SHA hosted release assets and provenance
